cohort: 247 pregnant women diagnosed with oligohydramnios in the 3rd trimester and 247 healthy pregnancies
finding: Idiopathic disorder, congenital anomalies, preeclampsia/hypertension, and diabetes mellitus were associated with oligohydramnios in the 3rd trimester, which resulted in higher rates of operative delivery and cesarean section due to pathological CTG and fetal distress, as well as increased NICU admissions for observation, congenital anomalies, RDS, IUGR, meconium aspiration, and HIE.
